draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Marayoor! This is the only place in Kerala with natural sandalwood forests. The hills around you also hold ancient dolmens and rock paintings from the Stone Age.
draft.hungryLine: I don't have a named eatery to send you to up here, so find a small Kerala meals place in town and ask what's fresh today.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Look around Marayoor for the sandalwood forests and the old dolmens, then take SH 17 to Munnar, 42 km south.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a quiet spot near the sandalwood trees. At about 990 metres up, it's a calm place to sit.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Marayoor claims to be part of a Stone Age civilisation going back as far as 10,000 BC.

legends.title: As old as 10,000 BC
legends.body: Marayoor claims to belong to a Stone Age civilisation that's as old as 10,000 BC. Later came an age of large-scale dolmen building.

legends.title: Five villages
legends.body: Migrants from the old Pandya lands founded five villages here: Kanthalloor, Keezhanthur, Karayur, Marayur and Kottakudi. Together they were called the Anju Nadu.

tips.title: Expect rain.
tips.body: Kerala gets rain for at least seven to eight months a year, so keep a rain jacket handy in the hills.

tips.title: Use SH 17.
tips.body: Marayoor sits on the state highway that links Munnar with Udumalpet in Tamil Nadu.

story.title: Stone Age roots
story.body: Marayoor claims to be part of a Stone Age civilisation. Its rock paintings and dolmens date back to that age.

story.title: The dolmen builders
story.body: A later period saw dolmens built here on a large scale. They are part of what makes Marayoor so old.

story.title: The Anju Nadu
story.body: When the Madurai king Bangaru Thirumala Nayak was defeated by Chanda Saheb, people from ancient Tamilakam moved here. They set up five villages, the Anju Nadu.

story.title: A small panchayat
story.body: Marayoor panchayat had 12,399 people in 3,307 households, and Marayoor is its only village.

story.title: Smell the sandalwood
story.body: Walk near the sandalwood forests and look for a dolmen. Tell me how old you think it is.
